extracted.intended_audience: readers interested in theatre, acting, and American cultural biography
extracted.subtask_description: Normative criteria and standards for acting, dramatic art, and the civic-cultural role of the stage as expressed in a biographical/critical essay on Edwin Forrest. Focuses on qualities of performance, moral character, national spirit, and the social purpose of theatre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Americanism as a defining artistic quality
rubrics_metrics.description: From the beginning to the end of his career he was intensely American in his sympathies, his prejudices, his training, his enthusiasm for the flag and name of his country, his proud admiration for the democratic genius of its institutions, his faith in its political mission, his interest in its historic men, his fervent love of its national scenery and its national literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Americanism is presented as a positive, formative trait in an actor: it colors repertory choices, theatrical persona, and public reception. The passage contrasts this spirit with exaggerated dislike of aristocratic Old World usages and implies that an actor embodying national democratic ideals has special cultural significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and rejection of mechanical stage traditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Boldly rejecting the mechanical traditions of the stage, shaking off the artificial trammels of the established schools of his profession, he looked directly into his own mind and heart... struck out a style of acting which was powerful in its personal sincerity and truth, original in its main features, and, above all, democratic and American in its originality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance judged by independence from rote conventions, by personal sincerity and truth, and by forging an original style rather than conforming to established schools. The writer praises actors who develop inwardly derived modes of expression instead of mechanical mannerisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assertion of the sovereignty of the individual in performance
rubrics_metrics.description: All his great parts set in emphatic relief the intrinsic sovereignty of the individual man, the ideal of a free manhood superior to all artificial distinctions or circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative emphasis on performances that foreground personal dignity, defiance of unjust authority, and the moral superiority of authentic human worth. Examples: Tell confronting Gessler, Spartacus before the Emperor, Metamora scornful of the Englishman—roles where genuine virtue eclipses titular rank.

rubrics_metrics.name: Versatility, detachment, imagination, and emotional range
rubrics_metrics.description: The true player is the most detached, versatile, imaginative, and emotional style of man, most capable of understanding, feeling with, and reproducing all other styles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A top actor is judged by psychological detachment (to inhabit others), versatility across character types, rich imagination, and the emotional capacity to reproduce varied human styles. This versatility also equips the actor to mediate between social groups and reconcile differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatic art's civic and educative function
rubrics_metrics.description: Among the public agencies of culture destined to educate the American people out of their defects and faults into a complete accordant manhood--the dramatic art will have an unparalleled place of honor... it will become more and more influential as it learns to exemplify the various ideals of human nature and human life...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The stage is evaluated not only artistically but by its social utility: its capacity to teach, to exemplify ideals, to reconcile classes and creeds, and to present serious moral instruction disguised in entertainment. This is contrasted with the declining dogmatic Church; drama should clear itself of abuses to fulfill this role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral fibre and personal conduct supporting professional standing
rubrics_metrics.description: His sense of honor and his memory of his mother kept him from doing anything which would destroy his self-respect and give him a bad conscience... The good, strong, consecrated stock, both national and personal, they gave their boy... was of inexpressible service to him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An actor's personal morals, restraint from vices, filial and fraternal virtues, and general conduct are criteria for judging their career sustainability and public esteem. Exemplary private character is presented as foundational to professional success and reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ancestral and hereditary influences on character and talent
rubrics_metrics.description: The formation of the character and the shaping of the career of any man the circumstance of supremest power is the ancestral spirits which report themselves in him from the past... The law of heredity is... working in every point of plasma, every fibril of nerve, every vibration of force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation of a performer's qualities includes consideration of inherited national and personal traits (e.g., Scottish courage and tenacity, German reasoning and poetic sentiment) and parental example; heredity and upbringing are treated as significant explanatory and constitutive factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assimilation and intermingling as means to national and cultural improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: There are but two methods to this end: one, the intermingling of the varieties in generative descent; the other, the personal assimilation of contrasting experiences and qualities by mutual sympathetic interpretation and assumption of them. This latter process is the very process and business of the dramatic art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two processes—biological intermingling and cultural-personal assimilation—are presented as standards for producing a cosmopolitan national character. Dramatic art is explicitly praised as the chief practical vehicle for the latter: actors and plays that foster sympathetic understanding are socially valuable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civic-minded progressiveness and critique of complacent conformism
rubrics_metrics.description: They think too meanly and haltingly of the truth and good which are not yet established and fashionable... The best critics from abroad, and the wisest observers at home, agree that the most distinctive vice in the American character is described by the terms complacent rashness and assumption... The desideratum is to construct out of the alienated races and classes... a new type of character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultural outputs (including theatre) and citizens are evaluated by willingness to aspire to higher standards rather than to accept respectability or vulgar prizes. The passage calls for art and public life that resist complacency and cultivate an 'unflinching spirit of progress.'
